result.title: Seeing Through Distractions: Context-Stable Attribution via the Least Core
result.summary: Shapley-value-based explanations are widely used for feature attribution in machine learning. However, in computer vision, a feature may reduce the target-class score when added to the complete genuine image, even when the predicted label remains unchanged. We formalize such features as contextual distractors and investigate their attributions under semivalues and the least core. Under a weak average marginal monotonicity assumption, we derive quantitative semivalue--least-core gap bounds and sufficient conditions based on the probability of sampling smaller contexts. We further show that shifting semivalue weights toward larger contexts decreases the signed gap. Finally, controlled image-classification experiments and evaluations on Salient ImageNet provide strong empirical support for our theoretical findings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将完整图像中会降低目标类分数、却不改变预测标签的特征定义为 contextual distractor，在 semivalue 与 least core 框架下分析其归因，推导差距界与采样条件，并用图像分类及 Salient ImageNet 实验验证。
